title: Wait for one another (1 Corinthians 11:17–34)
hook: at their suppers some eat first and some go hungry; Paul hands on the words of the Lord's Supper
tomorrow: can a foot quit the body? Paul lets one try.

segments.voice: Yesterday's word: a way of escape, a door that comes with the temptation. Today the trouble isn't a pull. It's dinner.

Every potluck has an early crowd. They fill their plates with the good stuff, and whoever comes off the late shift finds a spoon in an empty dish and a paper plate. Corinth had it worse, and at church, at the Lord's Supper, a meal that was meant to be holy and shared. "For in eating every one taketh before other his own supper: and one is hungry, and another is drunken." Paul has been praising them. Now he stops: "I praise you not."
screen: `THE EARLY CROWD.` → `ONE IS HUNGRY, ANOTHER DRUNKEN.` → `I PRAISE YOU NOT.`

segments.voice: Paul is sharp: "What? have ye not houses to eat and to drink in? or despise ye the church of God, and shame them that have not?" Then he hands on what he says he received: "the Lord Jesus the same night in which he was betrayed took bread," gave thanks, broke it, and said, "Take, eat: this is my body, which is broken for you: this do in remembrance of me." Then the cup. Then a warning about eating "unworthily," "not discerning the Lord's body." Which body? Here Christians read it two ways, and both have a real case. Some, among them Catholic and Orthodox Christians, hear the bread. Christ is truly present in it, so eating carelessly misses him. Their best case: Paul has just quoted, this is my body; the word points straight back to the bread. Others, among them some Protestant readers, hear the people. The church is the body, and a chapter later Paul says so. Their best case: the failure Paul names here isn't bad manners at the altar. It's shaming the hungry. Some hold both at once. Paul's fix serves either reading: "Wherefore, my brethren, when ye come together to eat, tarry one for another." And if you're starving? "let him eat at home."
screen: `SHAME THEM THAT HAVE NOT?` · `THIS DO IN REMEMBRANCE OF ME.` · `THE BREAD, OR THE PEOPLE?` · `TARRY ONE FOR ANOTHER.` · then, large: `DISCERN THE BODY.`

segments.voice: Pour a glass of water, or picture one in front of you. Before you drink, wait. Hold the glass, and let the people who'd share your table this week come to mind: the late one, the quiet one, the one who eats less. Then take one slow sip, as if every one of them already had a plate.
Wait for one another. Paul's plain fix for a holy meal that had split the full from the hungry.
Your line: discern the body. Some hear the bread, some the people, and Paul's fix serves both. That's today.

howItsDone: Christians share the Lord's Supper, also called communion or the Eucharist, using Paul's words from this chapter; churches differ on how often and on how Christ is present in the bread and cup.

fork.reveal: the bread reading leans on the words right before the warning: take, eat: this is my body. the people reading leans on the shamed hungry. some readers hold both.

chat.meaning: Corinth's meal split the full from the hungry, and Paul said tarry one for another. However a church reads 'the body', the people at the table count.

notes: Debate shape: two readings of 'not discerning the Lord's body' (11:29) are each given their best case without ranking: the bread (Catholic and Orthodox Christians 'among them'), the gathered church (some Protestant readers 'among them'), and some who hold both. Lutheran, Anglican and other readings are not named; a Keeper should confirm the attributions are fair and not too narrow.
The index hook says 'the rich eat first'; 11:21–22 speaks of those who eat first and 'them that have not'. The lesson keeps to the text's wording and does not say 'rich'.
11:27–29 is paraphrased ('a warning about eating unworthily'); the KJV has 'damnation' in 11:29. Some texts read 'the body' without 'Lord's'; the lesson quotes the KJV and makes no manuscript claim.
'Let him eat at home' (11:34) is introduced with 'if you're starving'; the verse begins 'if any man hunger'. Confirm the paraphrase.
Grace storyline (days 1541–1554), day 3: the first supper night; the crew ate in the kitchen before guests had plates, and Pop noticed. Practice kind: taste (a slow sip).
